_status: DRAFT content for the no-typing conversation reset (docs/06 Part A). Revise after the Stage 1 interviews (docs/04 D1) so the cards use people's own words. The qualified reviewer approves every string before the Stage 3 live tool. Checked by src/content/content.test.ts. Used by the v0 prototype (docs/12 R0) and later by the Stage 3 app, so there is one source of truth.

worries.label: What it means for my job

types.label: Giving hard feedback

cards.text: What I'd like to happen next

steps.title: Choose your first sentence
steps.detail: Pick one to start with. Fill in the brackets in your head.

steps.title: Pick your one example
steps.detail: One recent, specific example is clearer than five.

steps.title: Decide what you'd like to happen next
steps.detail: One change you'd like to see, and by when.

openers: I'd like to talk about [the report]. I want to be straightforward because I think you can fix it.
Can we take 15 minutes? I want to give you some feedback on [the project].
I noticed [what happened]. I'd like to understand what got in the way.

types.label: Asking for something

cards.text: What I can offer in return

steps.title: Choose your first sentence
steps.detail: Pick one to start with. Fill in the brackets in your head.

steps.title: Name one specific ask
steps.detail: A number, a date or a decision. Specific is easier to say yes to.

steps.title: Plan your answer to "not now"
steps.detail: Decide in advance: "Can we agree when to come back to it?"

openers: I'd like to ask for [more time on the launch]. Can I explain why?
I want to talk about [my workload]. I have a specific suggestion.
Before [the planning meeting], can we discuss [the extra help]?

types.label: Responding to criticism

steps.title: Choose your first sentence
steps.detail: Pick one to start with. Fill in the brackets in your head.

steps.title: Prepare one clarifying question
steps.detail: For example: "Can you give me an example so I understand?"

steps.title: Give yourself time
steps.detail: It's fine to say: "Let me think about that and come back to you tomorrow."

openers: Thanks for telling me. Can you give me an example so I understand?
I want to get this right. What would good look like to you?
I hear you. I'd like to think about it and come back to you by [tomorrow].

types.label: Saying no

cards.text: The words I use to say no
What they decide to do next

steps.title: Choose your first sentence
steps.detail: Pick one to start with. Fill in the brackets in your head.

steps.title: Decide what you can offer instead
steps.detail: A later date, a smaller version, or someone else who can help.

steps.title: Say it once, then stop
steps.detail: A clear no with one reason is enough. You don't need to over-explain.

openers: I can't take on [the new report] this week. I can do it by [the 20th].
I'd like to help, but I need to say no to [this]. What I can do is [that].
Thanks for thinking of me. I'm not able to [take this on] right now.

types.label: Something else

cards.text: What I want to come out of it
What I'll do if it goes badly

steps.title: Choose your first sentence
steps.detail: Pick one to start with. Fill in the brackets in your head.

steps.title: Decide your one goal
steps.detail: Finish this sentence in your head: "It goes well if..."

steps.title: Pick a time and place
steps.detail: Somewhere private, when neither of you is rushing.

openers: I'd like to talk about [this]. Is now a good time, or later today?
Can we find 15 minutes? There's something I want to discuss.
I want to be open with you about [this].
